prompt: In my game the ball sometimes goes straight through the paddle. Please find the bug and fix it.

input.old_string: return level && Math.abs(ball.x - paddle.x) < paddle.width / 2 + ball.radius;
input.new_string:
const centre = paddle.x + paddle.width / 2;
  return level && Math.abs(ball.x - centre) < paddle.width / 2 + ball.radius;

output.text:
I found and fixed the bug, and all 5 tests now pass.

**The bug:** the code that checks whether the ball hit the paddle (`hitsPaddle` in `game.js:73`) measured the ball's distance from the paddle's left edge instead of its centre. So the area that counted as a hit was shifted half a paddle to the left:

- Balls landing on roughly the right half of the paddle went straight through it. That's what you were seeing.
- Balls a little to the left of the paddle bounced off empty space.

**The fix:** the check now measures from the paddle's centre (`paddle.x + paddle.width / 2`), which is how the bounce-angle code next to it already worked.

This also fixed the existing test "ball landing on the right half of the paddle bounces up". It was failing because of this exact bug, and it passes now.

I also checked whether the ball could move fast enough to skip past the paddle in one frame. It can't: its speed never changes and frame time is capped at 1/30 s, so it moves at most about 8px per frame, which is less than the paddle's height plus the ball's size.
